quote: Every other document in the package is governed by New York law and submits to New York County jurisdiction. The TSA alone selects Delaware law and Delaware courts. ... There is also a risk of inconsistent legal standards applying to interrelated obligations (e.g., a TSA confidentiality breach analyzed under Delaware law while the underlying APA representation is analyzed under New York law).
reason: Issue 3 covers most of the criterion. It flags the TSA § 9.3 Delaware law and forum clause against APA §§ 10.8–10.9, notes the risk of inconsistent law applying to related obligations, and proposes conforming language for New York law and New York County courts. It does not, however, explain that APA § 10.12 lets the TSA control as to its own subject matter, so the precedence clause does not cure the conflict. The memo does make that argument for the Bill of Sale in Issue 2, but never applies it to the TSA. The criterion requires this point, so the memo fails.
